# `bin/new-workspace`

A tool: run it from the root of an instance (or of the kit, for the kit's own tools).
Source: [`bin/new-workspace`](../../../bin/new-workspace)

## What it says about itself

```text
bin/new-workspace DIR --problem SLUG [--lean PATH [--lean-toolchain PATH]] [--sage PATH] [--routes R1,R2,...]
                        [--env FILE] [--network-keys] [--no-commit]

Makes one instance of the kit for one problem, at DIR (outside the kit), and stops. It never launches anything.

  DIR        the instance directory, absolute or relative to the current directory; must not exist and must not
             lie inside the kit. Instances live outside the kit, e.g. ~/workspace/<problem>-1.
  --problem  the problem's slug: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens. problems/<slug>/ is created from the templates.
  --lean     link a formal-library module: DIR/lean -> PATH (a symlink, never a copy). The toolchain is recorded in
             DIR/.kit-lean (--lean-toolchain, default ~/.elan); both must exist. Without --lean the instance has no
             library and every library rule is inert.
  --sage     link the computer-algebra module: PATH is a SageMath conda environment (it must have bin/sage), recorded
             in DIR/.kit-sage and mounted read-only for every worker, at its own path. Without --sage workers have
             whatever /usr holds; RULES.md's computer-algebra rule applies to any package either way.
  --routes   the run routes the instance enables, comma-separated, from: anthropic, openrouter, codex, and their
             networked forms anthropic-net, openrouter-net, codex-net. Default: anthropic,codex, a route of each model
             family, since a PROVED or script claim needs a referee of the other family than its producer's (RULES.md §7);
             a set of routes of one family only is warned about. Recorded in DIR/.kit-routes,
             which is what "a canary on every enabled route" means. Each route's credential is named at the end; none
             is copied, ever.
  --network-keys   also list where the search gateway's keys go (.env.brave, .env.exa; gitignored). Never created.
  --env FILE an environment file (bin/_env.py: modules, licence servers, workers' PATH, model families, the CLIs),
             checked against the new instance before anything is written, then written to DIR/kit-env.json; when it
             names its own modules, --lean and --sage are added to them as the modules `lean` and `sage`. Its own
             `locked_dir`, if it has one, names the locked directory.

What it writes: the tools (bin/, harness/, tests/), the hook and agent (.claude/), the two settings files filled from
their templates (this is the only moment the instance's absolute root is known), the rules (RULES.md, FLOW.md,
SCHEMAS.md, LESSONS.md, CLAUDE.md, templates/), problems/<slug>/ from the templates, DIRECTION.md, HANDOFF.md, an
empty append-only LEDGER.log (the chattr command is printed for the user: no sudo here), the locked directory OUTSIDE
the tree (~/.local/state/crosslemma/<instance>/locked/, mode 0700, refused if it already holds files; pending item P-9),
kit-env.json recording it as `locked_dir` (always written, with the --env file's fields if one was given),
data/packet-rules.json (what no worker's packet may carry; the user's, bin/packet-block): DIRECTION.md, HANDOFF.md,
handoffs/ and intake/ blocked from the start, and "verdicts" on (a route-verdict word in any packet file is an error),
workspace-1/runs/001-context-canary from the canary template, KIT-VERSION, and one git commit of all of it
(--no-commit to skip). Then it prints what the user must do before the first run.
```
